prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: hospital automated medication dispensing/returns: order intake, pharmacy review/prep/verification, cold chain, tube transport, ward receipt/cabinets, returns. Aliases: Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer. Elements: Medication Order Gateway (validates orders; flags missing/duplicate/conflicting data; Order Reconciliation Snapshot; order status; routes to review). Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot (prepares authorized orders; Priority Refill Tote Tag; presents package to Verification Station). Pharmacy Verification Station (final check; records outcome; blocks incomplete release; Batch Release Note). Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler (temperature records; reports excursions/connectivity loss; displays current temperature and excursions to staff). East/West Tube Dispatch Consoles (route availability; monitor capsules; Tube Route Exception Ticket). Pneumatic Tube Network (accepts only compliant loads; segment unavailable until tested). North/South Ward Cabinet Controllers (record arrival time and destination cabinet; North uses Priority Refill Tote Tag to confirm ward before tote acceptance; states Ready for Dispense, Out of Service). Medication Return Kiosk (guides return-bin checks, records outcomes; Return Bin Audit Label, used by Pharmacy Technician to identify bins for collection). Actors: Clinical Pharmacist (Dose Exception Review Slip). Pharmacy Technician (prep; ID checks; Cold Chain Handoff Card). Medication Safety Officer (Diversion Review Packet). Registered Nurse (verifies load intended for ward; checks refrigerated handling conditions; confirms return eligibility, separated from waste). Charge Nurse (Cabinet Downtime Notice). Hospital Courier (Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record). Biomedical Engineer, IT Operations Specialist, dispatch/operations/ward staff. Requirements: discrepancies block prep; release linked to order ID, package ID, time, credentials; canceled/duplicate/superseded held; manifest; capsule IDs/destination reconciled before admission; route/packaging problem holds load until resolved/documented; if automated transfer unavailable staff keep custody, alternate procedure; receiving confirms arrival, reports discrepancies; ward receipt check: packaging damage/moisture/tampering, IDs legible vs task list, quantity/descriptions vs receipt record; mismatched loads isolated, never in active stock; accepted items staged until placement authorized; receipt completion recorded; return bins checked intact/clean/correct stream,

New part:
S118: Staff reconcile the bin contents with the return entry before the bin is closed.
S119: Questionable or damaged returned medication is segregated and referred for review rather than combined with accepted returns.
S120: A checked return bin remains secured in its designated holding location until collection is authorized.
S121: The Hospital Courier collects only bins that are closed and recorded as ready for collection.
S122: The Charge Nurse ensures that unresolved receipt or return discrepancies remain assigned for follow-up at shift handover.
S123: A dose exception is any mismatch, omission, duplicate request, or clinically implausible value detected before a medication is released for use.
S124: The affected transaction remains on hold until an authorized reviewer documents a disposition.
S125: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot stops the affected pick sequence and keeps the package in a controlled hold location pending review.
S126: Cinderwake preserves the scanned product and quantity data associated with the exception.
S127: Juniper compares the active order with the scanned product, strength, and measured quantity, and blocks verification when a field differs.
S128: Pharmacy Verification Station uses the review slip to record the exception category, evidence checked, disposition, and reviewer identity.
S129: The Clinical Pharmacist assesses dose, route, timing, and patient-specific clinical concerns before approving a correction or rejecting the order.
S130: A correction requires a valid authorized order and must not be inferred from prior dispensing history.
S131: Larkspur keeps the cabinet transaction locked and confirms that the medication has not been administered while review is pending.
S132: The Registered Nurse escalates an urgent patient-care concern to the Clinical Pharmacist and follows the hospital's clinical response procedure.
S133: The Registered Nurse does not bypass a hold or substitute a product to clear an exception.
S134: The Charge Nurse assigns unresolved exceptions to a named role and confirms that ownership is maintained at shift handover.
S135: The Pharmacy Technician may gather package and transaction evidence but may not make a clinical dose decision.
S136: The Medication Order Gateway rejects incomplete or internally inconsistent order updates and retains the rejection reason for review.
S137: The North Ward Cabinet Controller prevents access to a held transaction until an authorized disposition is recorded.
S138: The South Ward Cabinet Controller reports a failed lock or an unrecognized access attempt for immediate operational review.
S139: The Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler reports excursions that could affect medication suitability, and affected stock remains unavailable pending assessment.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
